summary: Norman Mosley Penzer was an Indologist who earned an M.A. from the University of Cambridge around 1910–1913. By 1925, he was a member of the Folklore Society and Royal Asiatic Society, and a Fellow of several British learned societies.

Norvin J. Hein worked in Indology and religious studies, having studied under Franklin Edgerton. By 1965, he served as Associate Professor of Comparative Religion in the Divinity School at Yale University.

Buddhist studies scholar Nosei Fuji studied as an exchange student at Dongguk University in 1986. He lectured at Daegu University in 1988, directed the Buddhist Cultural Institute at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College, and became a professor at Ryukoku University.

Notto R. Thelle works in religious, Buddhist, and Japanese studies. After serving at the NCC Center for the Study of Japanese Religions and the University of Oslo (~1986–2006), he earned degrees in Oslo and became section head at Oslo Metropolitan University.

Noémie Verdon is a scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Lausanne by 2015 under Johannes Bronkhorst and Charles Genequand, and was affiliated with Kyoto University in 2018–2019.

Noël Peri was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Sinology who studied at the Séminaire de Saint-Sulpice (~1883–1888). He taught Western music at Tokyo University of the Arts and later served at the École française d'Extrême-Orient.

Nyanaponika Thera was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Nyanatiloka Mahathera, Anton Walter Florus Gueth, and Mahasi Sayadaw, and attended the University of Peradeniya. He founded and led the Buddhist Publication Society and served as principal of the Forest Hermitage.

Nyingcha Duoji is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at Boston University and earned a PhD from Harvard University, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp and teacher Mark Elliott.

Nyo Shul Lungtok Tenpé Gyaltsen studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He also taught Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Nyoshul and Katok monasteries and under teachers including Dudjom Rinpoche, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, mentoring numerous prominent students.
Nyoten Jinbo was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Baisen Azegami and served as a professor at Komazawa University.

Odette Viennot was an Indology and archaeology scholar who studied at the École du Louvre and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Philippe Stern. She worked at the Guimet Museum and the National Centre for Scientific Research (~1954–1978).
Odolen Smékal was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Vincenc Pořízka and earned his PhD from Charles University in 1952. He began teaching Hindi at Charles University in 1954.
Ofer Peres is an Indology and religious studies scholar who has held posts at the South Asia Institute at Heidelberg University and at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem.

Ogyen Trinley Dorje works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche, Pema Donyo Nyinje, Drub Pön Dechen Rinpoche, the 14th Dalai Lama, Dragpa Tenpa Yarpel, and Bokar Rinpoche, and taught Khenpo Sherab Püntsok.
Ohryu Matsushima is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at and held a post at Ryukoku University.

Oktiabrina Volkova worked in Indology and Buddhist studies after studying at Saint Petersburg State University and under Bidia Dandaron. She taught at the Moscow State Institute of International Relations and was a researcher at the Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies.

Olaf Hansen was an Iranian and Central Asian linguistics scholar who earned his doctorate and completed his habilitation at the University of Hamburg under Hans Reichelt. He held posts at Berlin, Jena, and served as Professor of Indo-Iranian at FU Berlin.

Olav Hackstein is a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Freiburg and the University of Pennsylvania, and in 2008 became professor of historical and Indo-European linguistics at the University of Munich.

Oldřich Friš was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD from Charles University under Vincenc Lesný, also studying in Berlin. He served as acting professor at Palacký University Olomouc and as assistant professor and language section director at Charles University.
